g1-implement.title: Stored spine origin + engine-native isolation: implement
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for this gate and dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-implementer. BOTH HALVES LAND IN THIS ONE GATE -- they are not separable, because the read side is inert without the stamp and would report green while doing nothing. Half one (write): scripts/init_work_area.py stamps a top-level `origin` block carrying `worktree` when instantiate_spine writes a spine. Half two (read): scripts/checklist_engine.py gains a PURE refusal-or-None function comparing the spine's origin.worktree against the engine's OWN Path.cwd(), called from ONE site in main() after load() and BEFORE dispatch(), refusing WITHOUT persisting; a spine with no usable origin falls back to today's behaviour. Half three (docs): docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md documents `origin` as a top-level key. Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT: `attach g1-implement --type implementer-result --field status=complete`.

constraints: SHAPE (from the converged design, PLAN_ALTERNATIVES.md candidate B): a pure function `origin_worktree_refusal(spine: dict, *, cwd: str, verb: str) -> str | None`, no filesystem, no clock, no subprocess -- matching the repo's existing refusal-or-None precedent spine_lifecycle.closeout_refusal. The impure caller lives in main(), immediately after `cl = load(path)` and BEFORE `dispatch(...)`, and passes cwd=str(Path.cwd().resolve()).

REFUSE WITHOUT PERSISTING. main() saves on the EngineError path for every verb except `current`, so a refusal raised inside dispatch() would write into the very tree the guard protects, and would clobber a concurrent legitimate writer with a spine loaded before the refusal. The guard must print its refusal and return non-zero WITHOUT calling save().

Engine-native, never a forwarded cwd. The engine reads its own Path.cwd(). It must NOT pass cwd= to a subprocess check. Forwarding the stored root into verify_worktree_isolation.py --here makes the comparison X == X, because origin.worktree and the EXPECTED value in the check text both derive from the same resolved root at creation.
The resolved root is carried in a name distinct from base_dir. base_dir is also the gauge path base and the --from-child base. Do not touch base_dir.

VERB SCOPE: guarded = MUTATING_VERBS | {"claim", "heartbeat"}. Exempt = {"current", "release"}. `current` is the only genuinely read-only verb and inherited doctrine has an invoker read a subordinate's `current` cross-tree for a REFRESH REQUESTED line. `release` is exempt deliberately as the single recovery escape hatch -- a lease on a spine whose worktree was removed at closeout must stay clearable, and a non-owner release already demands --force --reason on the record. Assert the guarded set as data in a test, both membership and non-membership.

CONTAINMENT, NOT EQUALITY. The refusal fires when cwd is neither the stored root nor inside it. Equality would refuse from <root>/scripts or <root>/.agent-work/<id>, which the check being superseded accepts -- verify_worktree_isolation compares `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, which succeeds from any subdirectory. Use Path.is_relative_to (already segment-wise) so a sibling sharing a prefix, e.g. /w/repo-2 against /w/repo, is NOT inside. Pin that sibling case with a test.

NORMALIZE BOTH PRODUCERS. spine_lifecycle.py:311 stores str(Path(worktree)) -- unresolved, native separators. init_work_area stamps Path(root).resolve().as_posix(). On Windows those are C:\a\b and C:/a/b for the same directory. Fold case and separators with os.path.normcase inside the pure function; leave symlink resolution outside it (stored side resolved at write time, cwd side at read time) so the function stays pure. Any case-folding assertion must be skipUnless(os.name == 'nt') rather than pretending it proves something on Linux.

EXHAUSTIVE FALLBACK. All of these take today's behaviour and must never raise: `origin` absent; `origin: null`; `origin` not a dict (a string or list -- .get would raise AttributeError, which main() does not catch); `origin: {}`; `worktree` absent; `worktree` empty; `worktree` not a string. validate_spine.py guards none of them -- probed and confirmed -- so the engine handles every shape itself.
scripts/spine_lifecycle.py gets ZERO changes. build_origin() and open_work() are already correct; the stamp must be key-compatible with build_origin's block (a subset of its keys).
scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py and scripts/agent_work_root.py must NOT be edited. If the change wants them, STOP and report -- it is a float, not a decision.

ADMIRAL AMENDMENT 2026-08-13 -- the four-file deletion is AUTHORIZED and must be taken, not floated. Delete init.c0 from skills/commander/templates/COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json AND retire scripts/verify_worktree_precondition_coverage.py together with its three enumeration tests, because that script asserts exactly the wiring being removed and goes 3 failed / 4 passed if the check alone is deleted. Once enforcement is engine-native, per-template coverage of a command check is the wrong question.

tests/test_worktree_precondition_wiring.py must stay green and its existing assertions must NOT be weakened. It is the merged tripwire. Its fixtures are all origin-less, so it is green by construction under this change and proves the FALLBACK only -- it is structurally blind to the new path. Do not lean on its greenness as proof the new behaviour works.

Never guess a field. init_work_area.py does not know branch, base, parent or the dispatching session -- omit them rather than emitting a plausible wrong value. Stamp exactly {work_id, worktree, opened_by: "init_work_area"}.

Every new check must be demonstrated FAILING in the defective world and PASSING in the healthy one, in the same test. A guard proven only on its pass side is the defect class this repo names 'a check that cannot fail'.

ADMIRAL AMENDMENT 2026-08-13 -- the in-process cross-tree caller. scripts/mcp_spine_server.py:361 calls checklist_engine.main() IN-PROCESS and never chdirs, so a cwd-comparing guard reads the MCP SERVER's cwd, not the spine's. spine_rail.py never subprocesses the engine and gauge_writer_hook.py never calls it, so this is the only real cross-tree caller. Handle it deliberately and state how.

ADMIRAL AMENDMENT 2026-08-13 -- a NEW test that exercises a spine actually CARRYING origin is an EXIT CRITERION, covering BOTH the match and the mismatch case, in a new file tests/test_spine_origin_isolation.py. tests/test_worktree_precondition_wiring.py is green by construction -- every fixture builds an origin-less spine -- so it is blind to this change and is evidence for the FALLBACK branch only.
ADMIRAL AMENDMENT 2026-08-13 -- the withdrawn overclaim. Do NOT restate 'non-forwardability' anywhere. Certify only: coverage, unbypassability from the spine, and an independent expected side.

status_detail.blocker: The guard collides with the in-process MCP caller and the collision is structural. spine_open creates a NEW worktree and stamps origin.worktree to it; the next verb on that spine is claim, issued in-process through the door at mcp_spine_server.py:361, which never chdirs; the door process cannot already stand inside a directory that did not exist a moment earlier. So spine_open then claim in one session is now impossible through the door, by construction. tests/test_mcp_lifecycle.py FullStdioRoundTripTests fails and is the only failure. Reproduced independently by the Commander and again by the reviewer. The Commander's own handoff reason 1 was false: run_crew.launch_process at scripts/run_crew.py:676 passes no cwd=, so a dispatched crew inherits the dispatcher's cwd, not its spine's worktree. Verb scope cannot fix it (the round trip drives start, attach and advance, all in MUTATING_VERBS). Having the door supply SPINE.parent's toplevel cannot fix it either: measured equal to the stamped origin.worktree by construction, which is the X equals X tautology this issue exists to avoid. Every honest fix changes who sets cwd, in run_crew.py or mcp_spine_server.py, both outside allowed scope and both production behaviour, which the launch order requires be floated.
status_detail.authority_needed: Commander commander-315-native; floated to the Admiral of epic 568
status_detail.next_action: Admiral rules on the collision: option 1, run_crew.launch_process passes cwd=<the spine's worktree>, correct on independent merits but does not fix spine_open then claim; option 2, the door chdirs around its in-process main() call, fixes both halves and costs mcp_spine_server its deliberate cwd-independence; option 4, accept the break only if spine_open then claim in one session is genuinely unsupported, which the test asserts it is not. Commander recommends 1 plus 2.
status_detail.resume_reason: Admiral ruling received: implement options 1+2 as a bounded addition to the reviewed change.

g1-review.title: Stored spine origin + engine-native isolation: review
g1-review.imperative: Fill templates/REVIEWER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-reviewer. The reviewer's jobs, in order: (1) THE TRAP -- prove the comparison is not a tautology, that its two sides come from independent sources, and that the refusing side genuinely fires; (2) THE ARM -- prove the new tests have a failing side by reverting each half and watching them go red, rather than trusting that they pass; (3) THE FALLBACK -- prove every origin-less shape is untouched and none raises; (4) THE NO-GOS -- no forwarded cwd, base_dir untouched, no write on the refusal path, spine_lifecycle.py and the two forbidden files unchanged, the tripwire's existing assertions not weakened, init.c0 and its coverage apparatus DELETED as the Admiral authorized on 2026-08-13 (verify_worktree_precondition_coverage.py and its three enumeration tests retired with it); (5) THE OVERCLAIM -- confirm nothing in the change or its artifacts claims non-forwardability. Wait for and integrate the returned REVIEW_RESULT. ADMIRAL AMENDMENT 2026-08-13: also (6) THE NEW COVERAGE -- confirm tests/test_spine_origin_isolation.py exercises a spine that actually carries origin, on BOTH the match and the mismatch side, and that test_worktree_precondition_wiring.py is NOT treated as coverage of the stamped path; and (7) THE IN-PROCESS CALLER -- confirm mcp_spine_server.py:361 (checklist_engine.main() in-process, never chdirs) is handled deliberately.
